comment: Another dollar on Individual and still no lossless, which is the part that bugs me. 320 is fine for AirPods and the car, but if they want more money they should be selling me a real hi-fi tier. Tidal's higher tier is already in roughly this range, so I'm going to compare specs before I accept a hike for the same audio.

Spotify raises prices and the artists still get fractions of a cent per stream. I already moved to Apple Music over royalties, and this price bump makes me less likely to come back out of habit. Not a single cent of this is going to the people making the music.

Cool, prices are going up while smart shuffle still sneaks random songs into my liked songs and CarPlay still only shuffles the liked ones. Paying more for a shuffle that doesn't shuffle is a hard sell. Fix the shuffle first.

A dollar more is fine by me. I've paid since 2018 and the Spotlight setup is worth it to me, even with features getting pulled and me waiting forever for new ones. Not going anywhere, though I'd love tabs to show up before they raise the price again.

A buck more for no ads is still worth it to me. I'm not cancelling, Premium is the one sub I never drop. My only hope is the email about the new price doesn't come with another round of renewal prompts when I try to cancel.

Ugh, another price bump. I'm on a student plan so mine barely moves, but the family and duo plans going up stings for people I know. Premium is still worth it for no ads and Connect, though when Tidal does better audio for about the same money I can see why people compare.

Price isn't really what I care about. I'm more annoyed the album radio option is gone and playcounts are hidden. Still, Spotify is the most feature-rich thing I've used, so a dollar doesn't move me much.

A dollar more is nothing if the home screen goes back to normal, but I'm not paying for a TikTok feed with giant cards. If the redesign stays I'm cancelling and going to Apple Music, the price bump is just salt in the wound. Fix the home screen.

Price going up while downloads still break after every update and support never fixed it. I'd want them to fix the app before they ask for more money. Rolled back to an older version again just to get it working.

They want more money for an app that keeps shoving podcasts and an AI DJ in my face. YouTube Music is honestly a great deal with a strong app. If the UI doesn't calm down I'm going to look hard at leaving.
Price going up? I already cancelled over the music tab redesign. Still the same awful card layout with no album tiles. Switching to Apple Music unless they turn the album tiles view back.

Raising prices and the heart button is still gone. 'Nickel and dime' is exactly right. I'd pay a small add-on to get the heart button back, but charging more while my playlist workflow stays broken is money grubbing. Apple Music is sitting right there.

Student plan going from $4.99 to $5.99 is still a steal with Hulu included, I guess. Still stings a bit since I'm broke and the Showtime perk is already gone. I'm not switching yet because I need the offline downloads for transit.

Spotify raises the price while the UI keeps getting more cluttered and there's still no lossless or Spatial Audio. By my math Apple Music is the better deal now. I'd probably switch back, Connect is the only thing keeping me here.

Doesn't affect me since I'm on free, but the free experience is still ads every few songs and shuffle only. Maybe I'd pay for Premium if it were cheaper, but at this price I'm sticking with free and YouTube for the rest.

A dollar more a month is still bang for the buck for me. I use it every day and the no-ads skips and offline listening make it worth every penny. My real gripe is ads creeping heavier and perks getting dropped without a price change.

Price doesn't matter to me much, I cancelled once over feature changes and the enhance feature and lost like button are still broken. Discover Weekly is the only reason I'm still here. Another dollar won't change my mind either way.
Going to $10.99 still feels fair for unlimited skips and no ads. I'd pay it. I still hate how free users get treated and the content restrictions, but Premium is absolutely worth it for me.

Fine, raise it, I'm mostly paying for ad-free music. But the home screen is already crowded with podcasts and the music filter is a pain. Price isn't the problem, the app is. One more bad update and I'm cancelling.

Paying more for Premium while the podcast ads still play for subscribers. That's paying for nothing. They keep shoving podcasts onto my home screen and library, and Overcast and Pocket Casts are right there. Gotta make money somehow, but this is ridiculous.

A dollar more for the best library around is fine by me. Discover Weekly still works for me, though the new UI makes it harder to find. Premium is still a good deal and I'm not going anywhere over this.
The price doesn't bother me much since I'm on the old version anyway. Still, if they force the new layout on me I'm cancelling the day it happens. Just want to listen to music, so keep it simple.

Family plan is still pretty cheap per person even at $16.99, so we're keeping it. My worry is being pushed onto a plan we don't need or losing playlists when they change plans. Works great for us so far.

The price doesn't matter to me, I already cancelled. What drives me nuts is the renewal pop-up that shows up every time I open the app, even after clearing cache and reinstalling. It started after an update and it's very frustrating.

A buck is nothing for ad-free skips, downloads and casting. Premium is still the last subscription I'd cancel. My only real complaint is the free tier keeps getting more restricted and the pop-up suggestions are annoying.

I'm fine paying more if the extra money actually goes to artists. Music is already absurdly cheap for what you get, but artists get almost nothing per stream. If Spotify says it's investing in the product, show me the artist payouts going up too.

Another price hike and still no lossless or HiFi tier. Tidal and Qobuz do hi-fi for similar money, so the gap is getting harder to justify. I'll keep Spotify for Connect and discovery, but Tidal is still the app I actually listen to for music.

The price is fine, my problem is the liked-song hearts still don't show on album or track lists. I'm not paying more for a worse way to track what I've liked. If this stays I'll be looking at Apple Music again.
